why: `ruvyxa.config` has three descriptions of one object, and only two of them
were ever held together. `ProjectConfig` in crates/ruvyxa_cli/src/config.rs
decides what the compiler reads; `CONFIG_KEY_SCHEMA` in
packages/ruvyxa/runtime/config-schema.mjs decides what the renderer accepts;
`RuvyxaConfig` in packages/@ruvyxa/core/src/types.ts decides what TypeScript
accepts. tests/packages/core/config-schema.test.ts held the second and third
level against each other, and nothing at all compared the first.
So `image.maxWidth` — declared `pub max_width: u32` with a default of 3840
and a documented `0` escape hatch, and declared `maxWidth?: number` in the
public type — was missing from the schema and from the hand-written literal
the schema test compares against. Both descriptions that were gated agreed
with each other and disagreed with Rust, so the gate saw nothing, and
`assertKnownKeys` threw `RUV1602 unknown config.image field: maxWidth`
before any command could run. Every command loads the config first, so a
project that set the documented option could not run `dev`, `build`,
`start`, `check`, `routes`, `analyze`, `doctor`, `clean`, `bench`,
`test:parity`, or `add`.
This file is the missing third edge. `config_surface_matches_the_rust_config`
in crates/ruvyxa_cli/src/tests.rs reads each field list back out of serde —
every one of these structs carries `deny_unknown_fields`, so it names the
fields it accepts in the error it raises for one it does not — and asserts
the table below equals it. `config-schema.test.ts` asserts CONFIG_KEY_SCHEMA
equals the same table in both directions. A key in Rust and not in the
schema is the defect above; a key in the schema and not in Rust is an option
the compiler silently ignores.
Field lists are sorted by code unit, and no field name is transcribed by
hand on the Rust side: a `#[serde(rename)]` that changes a wire name changes
the probed list in the same commit.

serde: The struct's own `deny_unknown_fields` error names every field it accepts.
`rustPath` is where the probe key is planted, relative to `rustType`; a
`[]` suffix means the segment is an array and the probe goes into element 0.
none: No Rust struct describes this section: Rust reads the whole block as one
opaque value and the JavaScript renderer owns its shape. `reason` says why.

reason: `ProjectConfig::_content` is `Option<serde_json::Value>`: the content
engine runs entirely in JavaScript and Rust only forwards the block. The
renderer's `assertKnownKeys(config.content, 'config.content')` is the only
reader of this shape.
Nested inside the opaque `content` block; see `config.content`.
Probed directly rather than through `image.onDemand`, because
`OnDemandImageOptions` is an `#[serde(untagged)]` enum over `bool` and
this struct, and untagged deserialization discards the inner error.
`ProjectConfig::markdown_enabled` is `Option<bool>`: Rust only needs to
know whether to start the persistent MDX bridge, and the executable
unified plugins stay in the JavaScript config module. The renderer
collapses the whole block to `true` before Rust ever sees it.
Probed directly rather than through `site.robots`, because `RobotsSetting`
is an `#[serde(untagged)]` enum over `bool` and this struct.
The only section behind two untagged layers: `RobotsSetting` wraps
`RobotsGenerationOptions`, whose `rules` field is the untagged
`OneOrManyRules`. Probed directly for that reason, which is also why the
struct is `pub(crate)` rather than private to
crates/ruvyxa_cli/src/site_discovery.rs.
Probed directly rather than through `site.sitemap`, because
`SitemapSetting` is an `#[serde(untagged)]` enum over `bool` and this
struct.
